newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Mostar peace depends on residents.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Mostar peace depends on residents.

text.p: The United States on Monday condemned a new upsurge in ethnic violence in the Bosnian city of Mostar but said it had "done as much as we can" to bring peace there.

"Mostar is a difficult issue, but the United States has done as much as we can ... But fundamentally, the Dayton (peace) agreements rest on the efforts of the people involved, the governments and also the civilians," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

Bosnian authorities imposed a curfew in the Croat-Moslem city of Mostar on Monday after one person was killed and 22 were wounded in ethnic violence in which Bosnian Croats fired shots toward Moslem pilgrims trying to visit a local cemetery.

"The United States condemns this violence. We are calling upon the Croatian authorities and the Croatian civilians involved to exercise maximum restraint and not to repeat this kind of aggressive activity," Burns told a news briefing.
He said the United States, as author and mediator of the Bosnia peace deal reached in Dayton, Ohio, in 1995, has given a "considerable amount of attention" to Mostar and would continue to do so.
But the people of Mostar are "the ones who have to ... make it live and make it durable. And we're calling upon them to do so," Burns said.
